checks.criterion: Customer selected pages 1-1 / 1-2 / etc → print-ready PDF contains only selected pages; invalid selections rejected (422)

checks.evidence: pytest: for specs 1-1,1,3,1-4,2,4,1-2,4,3,1 -> GET /orders/{id}/documents/{doc}/file?variant=print returned 200 with exact expected page sets; variant=original always returned [1,2,3,4]; invalid ranges (5,0-2,3-1,a,1-9) on /public/shops/{slug}/quote returned 422.

checks.criterion: Staff click Print/download: HTTP 200, no 'supprimé' error, no automatic print job created by download/status change alone

checks.evidence: pytest: GET .../file?variant=print -> 200 after upload/order/status=printing with no job created (GET /orders/{id}/print-jobs == [] and agent claim == []); only explicit POST /orders/{id}/print-direct creates a job, and agent receives only selected page(s).

checks.criterion: Files durable: new uploads storage_key starts 'gridfs:'; deleting backend/storage_private does not break reading
checks.name: test_documents_survive_local_disk_loss_and_live_until_pickup (test_document_lifecycle.py)
checks.evidence: pytest: document storage_key startswith 'gridfs:'; shutil.rmtree(STORAGE_DIR) executed; subsequent GET .../file?variant=original returned all 4 pages and ?variant=print returned the correct subset for two separate orders.

checks.criterion: Order status printing/ready/paid: document still accessible; hourly POST /api/cron/retention leaves it intact
checks.name: test_documents_survive_local_disk_loss_and_live_until_pickup (test_document_lifecycle.py)
checks.evidence: pytest: after status=ready, pay(card_terminal), and POST /cron/retention (Bearer WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET), GET .../file?variant=print still returned 200.

checks.criterion: Order marked picked_up: files deleted (410), order/payment/history still viewable
checks.name: test_documents_survive_local_disk_loss_and_live_until_pickup (test_document_lifecycle.py)
checks.evidence: pytest: POST /orders/{id}/status picked_up -> 200; GridFS file count for that key == 0; document status 'purged'; GET /orders/{id} shows purged_at set, payment_status != unpaid, history last entry picked_up; GET .../file -> 410.
